title: Impact of ChatGPT on Academic Performance among Bangladeshi Undergraduate Students
venue: International Journal of Research in Science & Engineering
extended_summary:
This paper examines how ChatGPT relates to academic performance among Bangladeshi undergraduate students, focusing specifically on the roles of plagiarism, creativity, and motivation. The study is motivated by concerns that while ChatGPT can support students with writing, coding, and academic tasks, it may also encourage dependency, reduce originality, and undermine academic integrity. The authors propose a conceptual model in which plagiarism influences creativity, creativity influences motivation, and these factors together relate to academic performance.

The study uses a quantitative online survey design. Data were collected from undergraduate students in public and private universities in Bangladesh using a purposive sampling approach and a 15-item structured questionnaire with 5-point Likert-scale items. Although the methodology section mentions 100 students, the results section reports 102 respondents included in the final analysis. The authors analyzed the survey data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS to test hypothesized relationships among plagiarism, creativity, motivation, and academic performance.

The context is higher education in Bangladesh during early 2023, when students had access to ChatGPT in its early public phase. The study was conducted online via Microsoft Forms over a very short data-collection window of three days. Participants were undergraduate students from both public and private universities, making the study cross-institutional rather than confined to a single campus.

The main conclusion is that plagiarism, creativity, motivation, and academic performance are significantly related in the authors' model. They report that plagiarism facilitated by ChatGPT is associated with creativity, creativity is positively related to motivation, and creativity, motivation, and plagiarism are all linked to academic performance. The authors argue that institutions should promote ethical and responsible use of AI tools, discourage overdependence on ChatGPT, and foster originality, creativity, and academic integrity among students.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational large language model chatbot used to generate text and respond interactively to user prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as an AI chatbot used by Bangladeshi undergraduate students, with perceived impacts examined in relation to plagiarism, creativity, motivation, and academic performance via survey and PLS-SEM.

findings.finding_summary: In a survey-based PLS-SEM study of Bangladeshi undergraduates, ChatGPT-facilitated plagiarism was positively associated with creativity (Plagiarism -> Creativity: Original Sample=0.275, T=1.784, p=0.037), and creativity was positively associated with academic performance (Creativity -> Academic Performance: Original Sample=0.173, T=1.840, p=0.034). However, plagiarism and motivation showed negative paths to academic performance (Plagiarism -> Academic Performance: -0.287, T=1.970, p=0.026; Motivation -> Academic Performance: -0.213, T=1.698, p=0.046).
findings.measure: Survey-based latent constructs in PLS-SEM: plagiarism, creativity, motivation, and academic performance

findings.finding_summary: The study reported a significant positive relationship between creativity and motivation among students using ChatGPT-related contexts (Creativity -> Motivation: Original Sample=0.492, T=5.992, p=0.000). Authors interpret this as students with greater creative abilities displaying higher academic motivation.
findings.measure: Survey-based latent constructs for creativity and motivation using 5-point Likert items analyzed with PLS-SEM

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical primary study, but it uses a purposive sample and cross-sectional self-report survey with PLS-SEM rather than an experimental or quasi-experimental design. Reliability is also weak for some constructs (e.g., plagiarism and motivation), which raises measurement concerns.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports mixed associations, including negative paths from plagiarism and motivation to academic performance, and does not provide standardized causal effect sizes or achievement test gains. Overall impact is unclear to negative rather than demonstrating a clear positive educational effect.
